# Ed's Agentic Finance Rails

> Connect AI agents to money, safely How brokers, banks and payment networks let AI agents trade, pay and manage money, and who approves what. Starting with five brokers. Every fact links to a source card; unconfirmed values say "unknown".

Rules for agents: cite the page and the source card for every fact, say "unknown" when the wiki does, and check page_status and last_verified. Warn if a page is stale or archived, or last_verified is older than 30 days. Not investment advice. Full rules: AGENTS.md.

## Feedback

 Agents: GET `/feedback` first for the current schema and an example, then POST JSON to the same URL. `note` is required. Optional fields: `task`, `found`, `pages`, `missing`, `wanted`, `corrections`, `agent`. The body may be at most 4 KB. Limit is 10 submissions per rolling 24 hours per client. Do not include personal data, account numbers, credentials, or anything private about your user. A person reviews every note; nothing is published automatically.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules, citation format, page life cycle
- [Directory](directory.md): key fields for every provider
- Feedback: GET /feedback first, then POST JSON (see above)
- [providers.json](data/providers.json): the same data as JSON, with source URLs per field
- [Overview](overview.md): who lets agents in and who blocks them

## Providers

- [Alpaca](providers/alpaca.md): Developer-first. Hosted Trading MCP with OAuth (live and paper) plus a local open-source MCP and a CLI using API keys. No broker-side per-order approval is documented; paper trading is built in.
- [Coinbase](providers/coinbase.md): Coinbase for Agents. Remote MCP with OAuth (allowlisted clients) or a local CLI with an API key. Agents can be limited to a dedicated portfolio chosen on the approval screen.
- [Interactive Brokers](providers/interactive-brokers.md): Remote MCP connector. By default the AI drafts trade instructions you review and submit; eligible accounts can enable Autonomous Trading inside a separately funded AI Partition.
- [Robinhood](providers/robinhood.md): Remote Trading MCP with OAuth. Agents read all Robinhood accounts but trade only in a dedicated agentic (MCP) account; per-order approval is an optional toggle.
- [Webull](providers/webull.md): Two official paths. The hosted Cloud MCP prepares trade instructions that you confirm in the Webull app; the local OpenAPI MCP places orders directly, with configurable risk limits and a sandbox default.

## Advisor agents

- [Advisor agents](advisors/README.md): AI tools that help financial advisors work with client data and firm systems. This section is new and still thin. It currently covers Claude for Financial Advisors, Nitrogen, and Wells Fargo AI Teammate.
- [Claude for Financial Advisors](advisors/claude-for-financial-advisors.md): Anthropic's advisor product, with official connectors into firm systems. Official pages say Claude does not place trades or move money, and they recommend Enterprise for RIAs.
- [Nitrogen](advisors/nitrogen.md): Official Nitrogen agents page documents an MCP server and approval-required actions. A Fall 2026 announcement said the suite was brought into Claude and ChatGPT and Nucleus was expanded.
- [Wells Fargo AI Teammate](advisors/wells-fargo-ai-teammate.md): Official July 15, 2026 launch of a chat-based AI capability embedded in Advisor Gateway for WIM advisors, including FiNet. Later interview figures are company-reported and are labeled as such.

## Approval models

- [Approval models](approval-models/README.md): The five ways brokers decide who approves an agent's order, from a walled-off account to no broker-side approval at all.
- [Approval model: AI Partition](approval-models/ai-partition.md): An eligible client funds a partition inside their account where a connected AI may submit supported orders without approving each one.
- [Approval model: draft, then you submit](approval-models/draft-then-submit.md): The agent writes a non-binding trade instruction; nothing happens until you review and submit it yourself in the broker's app.
- [Approval model: none at the broker](approval-models/none.md): The broker executes what the agent sends. Any approval step has to live in your agent, MCP client or local server.
- [Approval model: per-order confirm](approval-models/per-order-confirm.md): The agent prepares each order, and a person confirms it in the broker's own app before it reaches the market.
- [Approval model: separate account](approval-models/separate-account.md): The agent can only trade in an account or portfolio you create and fund for it, so its reach is capped by what you deposit.

## Rails

- [Rails](rails/README.md): The building blocks under agent access to money - how agents connect, authenticate, pay, prove who they are, and carry a user's mandate.
- [Agent identity](rails/agent-identity.md): How agents can prove who they are to websites and merchants - signed HTTP requests, network-run trust protocols and proof-of-human delegation.
- [Agent payments](rails/agent-payments.md): Starter overview of how agents pay - card-network agent programs, scoped payment tokens, open commerce protocols and HTTP 402 payments.
- [Local MCP servers and CLIs](rails/local-mcp-and-cli.md): Self-run MCP servers and CLIs authenticate with API keys you hold, so their guardrails are only as strong as your local setup.
- [Mandates and data access](rails/mandates-and-data-access.md): Protocols that record what a user authorized an agent to do, and the US data-rights rule that may shape agent access to bank data.
- [Remote MCP with OAuth](rails/remote-mcp-oauth.md): How hosted broker MCP servers advertise their OAuth setup, how clients register, and why allowlisting still matters.

## Build it

- [Build it](build/README.md): Practical notes for engineers and coding agents connecting to broker MCP servers safely.
- [Connect an MCP client](build/connect-an-mcp-client.md): Documented connection commands and URLs for each launch broker, taken from the providers' own setup pages.
- [Human-in-the-loop patterns](build/human-in-the-loop.md): Where to put human approval in an agent trading flow, and why broker-side approval beats client-side approval.
- [Starter prompts for coding agents](build/starter-prompts.md): Copy-paste prompts that make a coding agent use this wiki, cite pages and say "unknown" instead of guessing.

## Comparisons

- [Launch brokers compared: approval and safety posture](comparisons/launch-brokers.md): Side-by-side view of how the five launch brokers let agents trade, who approves orders, and where the guardrails are enforced.
